and as-of semantics

Aging is an exact retained projection, not a mutable balance. `as_of_date`
includes obligations recognized on or before that date and subtracts only active
allocations/write-offs whose effective date is on or before it. Later reversals
restore the amount from their effective reversal date; they do not rewrite an
earlier as-of result. Future-dated facts are excluded.

The snapshot records Tenant, direction, as-of date, obligation IDs, exact per-item
original/settled/written-off/outstanding amounts, due date, days past due when a
source supplied the date, undated status, totals, canonical hash and idempotency
key. It does not invent buckets. Any bucketed presentation remains blocked until
the Product Owner approves exact boundaries.

## 7. Correction, reversal, and reconciliation

Recognized obligations are not silently edited, voided or deleted. A source
correction requires a separately registered source-correction contract that
creates linked adjustment/reversal evidence and, when applicable, a linked
Accounting reversal. Settlement reversal and write-off reversal require a reason,
authorized actor, unique occurrence and an open applicable fiscal boundary if a
journal is involved. A cash refund is a separate Treasury movement.

AP/AR reconciliation retains exact as-of population, active allocation/write-off
IDs, source and journal identities, subledger totals, supplied posted GL control
totals, differences, exception facts and a canonical hash. It never posts,
adjusts, signs off or applies a tolerance. Missing mappings/journals are explicit
exceptions rather than fabricated balances.

docs\\architecture\\P3_S23_S27_ACTIVATIO.Q03:
— Write-off authority, permissions and separation

### Decision closed

The decision defines who may propose, approve and reverse an AP/AR write-off; which roles receive
the existing permissions by default; whether Self-Approval is ever allowed; and
whether authorization varies by amount or object scope. No monetary threshold is
currently approved.

### Options

| Option | Complete product choice | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A-Revised — Accepted Platform/Tenant policy governs Self-Approval/SoD (accepted)** | Keep `subledgers.writeoffs_propose` in the existing Accountant default set. Give `subledgers.writeoffs_approve` and `subledgers.writeoffs_reverse` **no default-role grant**; assign them explicitly through the existing authorization and object-scope model. The already accepted Platform/Tenant Self-Approval policy governs approval and reversal. Where applicable policy requires independent approval, proposer and approver must be different active authorized memberships. Self-Approval is absolutely prohibited only when the operation is explicitly classified as a Protected Operation under accepted platform policy; this decision does **not** classify write-off or reversal as Protected Operations. Introduce no monetary or cumulative threshold. Missing required authorization or Self-Approval configuration fails closed. | Approval and reversal services must evaluate the effective versioned policy and exact object scope inside the transaction. Every decision remains versioned and auditable and retains exact Accounting/subledger lineage. No role, position or source approval implies write-off authority. No numeric policy field or reversal-request schema is authorized by this decision. |
| B — Default senior-role approval | Accountant proposes; Owner/Admin receive approval and reversal by default; proposer and approver differ, but reversal is a single authorized action. No amount threshold. | Easier setup, but broad default grants expand financial authority and single-actor reversal provides weaker control. Role membership still cannot bypass object scope. |
| C — Threshold-based delegated authority | Permit Self-Approval or role-specific approval below an approved amount and require independent approval above it; apply equivalent bands to reversal. | Supports higher-volume operations but cannot be implemented until the Product Owner supplies exact amounts, inclusivity, currency/basis, aggregation window, object scope and fallback behavior. No values may be inferred. |

**Decision:** **Q03 = A-Revised — accepted.** It uses the permissions already
catalogued, preserves the accepted policy-owned distinction between Protected and
other business operations, and closes the product gate without inventing a number
or silently elevating write-off/reversal classification.

**Still deferred:** every monetary or cumulative threshold; automated/de-minimis
write-off; batch approval; tenant-authored approval formulas; legal/tax treatment;
collection or dispute policy; UI; and any default approval/reversal grant beyond
the selected option.

# BONIRA — AP/AR Write-off Policy Specification

Governed by `PD-015` and `PD-030`.

V1 SHOULD / NON-BLOCKING.

Write-off is a first-class auditable occurrence and never deletes the source Obligation/history.

Manual proposal requires source Obligation identity/version, proposed effect, reason/comment, audit identity and evidence where governed.

No automatic threshold/materiality rule is defined. Approval is required and comes from approved workflow assignment/permission, not job title.

Accounting recognition follows the Recognition Owner Matrix. Reversal/correction creates a new governed occurrence and preserves history.

`UNSPECIFIED WRITE-OFF POLICY — MANUAL/HELD, DO NOT INVENT`

approved_rules.PD015_SPEC024: Manual auditable write-off; approval from permission/assignment; new governed correction/reversal occurrence; retain original history; no thresholds
approved_rules.PD030_matrix: Subledgers owns write-off and reversal/correction recognition; L2 Accounting draft after approval; GL remains Accounting authority
approved_rules.P3_Q03_A_Revised: Existing explicit scoped approve/reverse permissions, no default grants, effective Platform/Tenant Self-Approval policy, independent memberships only where policy requires; no implicit Protected classification
approved_rules.P3_as_of: Effective dates govern retained as-of results; future-dated facts excluded; later reversal restores amount from its effective date

unresolved_material_contract: No inspected approved source specifies whether correcting an approved write-off is a full reversal plus replacement or an adjustment, or whether original reversal and replacement approval share one atomic effective-date boundary. These choices change outstanding balances and historical/as-of results; persistence authority does not select one.

proposed_bounded_resolution.mechanism: Full reversal of the prior approved write-off plus a separately approved replacement, never a delta or destructive overwrite
proposed_bounded_resolution.commit: At replacement approval, reverse the old decision and approve the replacement atomically; require existing explicit reversal and approval permissions and applicable versioned Self-Approval checks for both actions
proposed_bounded_resolution.effective_date: One explicit correction date used by both reversal and replacement, no earlier than prior write-off effective date; do not rewrite earlier as-of results; open applicable Accounting boundary where a GL effect is required
proposed_bounded_resolution.pending_and_denied: Original effect remains until successful atomic correction; rejected or unapproved replacement creates no financial effect; no cancellation behavior enabled without governing policy
proposed_bounded_resolution.lineage: Replacement retains exact predecessor decision, same tenant/obligation and source/version pins; no inferred historic pairing

implemented_before_semantic_stop: Nullable protected source predecessor relation and structural integrity/immutability only; no financial transition or policy activated
